title: Motivational Science
originAuthor: Jeffrey Gray, Charles Carver, Michael Scheier
summary: Behavior is organized around two fundamental motivational systems: approach (moving toward rewards, goals, positive outcomes) and avoidance (moving away from threats, punishments, negative outcomes). These systems have distinct neural substrates and produce different cognitive and emotional patterns.
tegBlueUsage: TEG-Blue maps approach/avoidance onto the Four-Mode Gradient as the fundamental orientation underlying all four states. Connection is approach-dominant (open, exploratory, reward-sensitive). Protection through Domination represent increasingly avoidance-dominant patterns (threat-focused, defensive, punishment-sensitive). The gradient tracks how avoidance can become chronic and self-reinforcing.

content.title: Core Concept
content.content: Gray's Reinforcement Sensitivity Theory proposes two systems: the Behavioral Activation System (BAS) driving approach toward rewards, and the Behavioral Inhibition System (BIS) driving avoidance of threats. Carver and Scheier extended this into self-regulation theory, showing how approach and avoidance orientations shape goal pursuit, emotional experience, and coping strategies. These are not choices but neurobiological orientations that can become trait-like through repeated activation.

content.title: How TEG-Blue Integrates This
content.content: TEG-Blue treats approach/avoidance as the motivational substrate of the Four-Mode Gradient. Connection represents balanced, flexible motivation with approach available. Protection activates avoidance appropriately. Control and Domination represent chronic avoidance orientation — where the system has learned that approach is dangerous and only threat-management strategies feel safe. Recovery involves gradually restoring approach capacity.
